subject: POC Prompt Set & Eval Dataset - next steps and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: POC Prompt Set & Eval Dataset - next steps and success criteria

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today - great to meet the AcmeHealth team. As promised, here's a short recap of next steps and the evaluation plan so we can kick off the POC smoothly. I've attached a one-page evaluation plan template for your convenience.

Summary / success criteria (proposed):
- Functional: Redwood answers >= 85% of the clinical triage prompts within the accepted answer set (we'll co-define pass/fail per prompt).
- Safety & compliance: No PHI leakage beyond expected de-identified fields; IDS/QA checks pass on sample logs.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency <= 600ms for the 512-token scenario on our Dedicated profile.
- Cost: Estimated token/unit cost within the agreed budget range (we'll share a cost estimate after we see the prompt mix).

Evaluation plan (high level):
1) Collect prompt set & anonymized logs from AcmeHealth (you) - preferred format: CSV with columns [prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_label/answer, context_meta]. Sample size: 1,000 prompts representative of production mix; we can start with a 200-prompt seed.
2) Redwood ingests and normalizes prompts; run baseline eval against open model variants and our recommended quantized runtime.
3) Run comparative evals and produce metrics: accuracy, F1 (if applicable), safety flags, latency distribution, token usage breakdown.
4) Joint review call to go over results, iterate, and decide go/no-go.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): Share sample prompts + 1 week of anonymized logs -> Sam/Priya
- Week 1: Redwood ingestion & baseline runs -> Dev/SE leads
- Week 2: Full evals and results -> Marissa & SE
- Week 3: Joint review & next steps / handoff to engineering if we proceed

Ownership:
- AcmeHealth: provide prompts, anonymized logs, expected answers, and security contact for SOC2/Security Qs -> Sam / Priya
- Redwood: ingestion, eval execution, metrics, and report -> Marissa (sales) and Dev (SE)

Action items for you:
1) Send a small sample prompt file (200 rows) + 1 week of anonymized logs (or export) - CSV/JSON preferred.
2) Flag any restrictions on data sharing (S3 upload, secure share, or preferred transfer method).
3) Share security/compliance contact so we can route SOC2 docs if needed.

Attachments: redwood_poc_evaluation_plan_template.docx (template)

If the above looks good, we'll stand up the ingestion run as soon as we receive the sample. Happy to adjust criteria/timeline - want to make this low-friction for your team.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

---
Attachment: redwood_poc_evaluation_plan_template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Prompt Set & Eval Dataset - next steps and success criteria

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. This looks good to us - we can start by sending a 200-row prompt sample and a week of anonymized logs by early next week. A couple quick items from our side:

- Attached are two sample files (acmehealth_prompts_sample.csv, acmehealth_logs_sample.json) for the format we have available today. The prompts file includes a short expected_answer column.
- Security: our security team asked for a SOC2 attestation and a short answers doc on data handling. I attached the security questions they often send vendors.
- Transfer method: we prefer S3 with pre-signed URLs or an encrypted transfer share (we can provision a temporary bucket).

We'll aim to get the sample files and the secure transfer link to you by Monday.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Carter | Head of NLP Engineering, AcmeHealth
sam.carter@acmehealth.com

---
Attachments: acmehealth_prompts_sample.csv, acmehealth_logs_sample.json, acme_health_security_questions.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Prompt Set & Eval Dataset - next steps and success criteria

Hi Sam / Marissa,

Appreciate the samples, Sam. I took a quick look at the prompts file and logs you attached - format looks OK. A few notes/questions so we can prep ingestion: 

- For the logs file, are the patient identifiers fully removed or are they pseudonymized? We need to confirm no PHI is shared.
- CSV encoding: UTF-8 is perfect. If there are any multi-line prompts, let me know whether they are newline-escaped or quoted.
- Preferred transfer: presigned S3 works well. If you send the presigned put URLs I'll verify we can pull them from our secure ingest service.

Next steps from SE: once we have the sample + transfer link I'll run a quick sanity ingestion and run the baseline eval (should take ~1 business day for the 200-row sample). Happy to join a 30-min sync - suggest Mon 10am PT if that works for you.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Prompt Set & Eval Dataset - next steps and success criteria

Great, thanks Sam and Dev. Quick summary and proposed concrete plan: 

1) Transfer: Sam to share presigned S3 put URLs (or secure share) by Monday morning.
2) Ingestion & baseline: Dev will run ingest + baseline eval on the 200-sample (target complete by Tue EOD).
3) Full run: After we validate the seed, we'll ingest the 1,000-prompt evaluation set and run the full metrics (target complete in Week 2).
4) Review: Schedule a 60-min review in Week 3 to go through metrics, safety flags, and recommendations.

Owners:
- AcmeHealth owner: Sam Carter (data delivery + security)
- Redwood owners: Marissa Cole (POC lead) and Dev Patel (technical lead)

Deliverables from Redwood:
- Ingestion report (mapping and any data quality notes)
- Eval report (accuracy, latency, safety checks)
- A short runbook with suggested next steps and config recommendations

Meeting: Dev suggested Mon 10am PT for a 30-min sync to kick off - Sam, does that work? If not, suggest 3 other windows and we'll pick one.

Next steps for you (Sam): share transfer link + security contact + any constraints by Mon EOD.

Looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa

From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmehealth.com>
